summary: Harry Potter game entries from the prepared 1000-title candidate queue, researched for Sami's fidelity-first archive route.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
entries.definitive_edition: Original Windows PC version for main route; PS2/GameCube/Xbox as secondary variant check

emulation.emulator: Not required for PC primary; PCSX2/Dolphin/Xemu only for console-variant comparison
emulation.notes: Use compatibility fixes for the PC release and keep platform variants clearly separated.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PC capture, with console emulation for variant comparison

primary.why: The 2001 Philosopher's Stone/Sorcerer's Stone game has meaningfully different platform versions. The PC version is a strong archive route for capture and one of the original-era versions, but console-specific versions should be treated as secondary comparison routes rather than assumed identical.
primary.how_to_play: Use the original Windows PC version for the main run, with compatibility fixes as needed. Add a separate PS2/GameCube/Xbox comparison if Sami wants the console-specific design covered.

secondary.exclusive_content: Different console-version design and presentation compared with PC/PS1/Game Boy versions
secondary.what_to_play: Run a targeted comparison or separate platform route if the archive wants all major Harry Potter 1 variants.
secondary.why: Licensed games from this era often differ substantially by platform, with multiple platform families existing.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
entries.definitive_edition: PlayStation 2 version for main route; PC and handheld versions as platform-variant comparisons

emulation.emulator: PCSX2 for PS2 primary if original hardware is unavailable
emulation.notes: Use accurate settings and avoid enhancements if documenting original presentation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS2 hardware or accurate PCSX2

primary.why: Chamber of Secrets has meaningfully different platform versions. The PS2 sixth-generation version is the strongest one-route console pick for fidelity and scope, while the PC, PS1, GBA, and GBC versions should be treated as separate variants if Sami wants full platform-variant coverage.
primary.how_to_play: Use a PS2 copy on original hardware or PCSX2 with accurate settings. Record platform, revision, controller, display settings, and whether PC/handheld variants were checked separately.

secondary.exclusive_content: Different PC design route from the console version
secondary.what_to_play: Play separately only if documenting the major PC variant.
secondary.why: The PC version is not simply a lower-fidelity copy of the PS2/Xbox/GameCube version.

secondary.platform: Game Boy Color / Game Boy Advance
secondary.what_to_play: Treat as separate comparison routes if handheld coverage matters.
secondary.why: Licensed games of this era often differ substantially by platform.

all_releases.reason: primary: best one-route fidelity/scope pick among the major platform variants.
secondary: preserve as a separate version if covering platform variants.

secondary.what_to_play: Compare only if documenting motion-control differences.
secondary.why: Wii controls can materially change the feel even when story content overlaps.

emulation.notes: Use native PC route; PCSX2/Dolphin/mGBA only for branch comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC with documented fixes, or original console hardware for console branch

primary.version: Original PC version with compatibility fixes documented
primary.why: Prisoner of Azkaban has meaningfully different PC, console, and GBA branches. The PC version is the strongest capture route for the classic EA adventure branch, while the PS2/Xbox/GameCube version should be logged separately if the console-specific structure matters.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned PC copy with compatibility fixes. Record OS, patch/fix state, resolution, controller/keyboard setup, character-switch progress, collectibles, and whether console/GBA versions were compared.

secondary.exclusive_content: Separate console branch by EA UK
secondary.what_to_play: Use if documenting the console version.
secondary.why: The console branch is not identical to the PC game.
It is a distinct Griptonite handheld version.

all_releases.fidelity: KnowWonder PC branch with best capture route.
all_releases.reason: primary: practical archive route for the classic PC adventure.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: PC, console, and GBA versions are distinct enough that platform must be logged.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record compatibility fixes, platform branch, controls, and collectibles.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, Part 1

emulation.notes: Use owned media; console emulation only for comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Owned PC/HD-console build with platform state documented

primary.why: Deathly Hallows Part 1 is an EA movie-tie-in action game with no normal current storefront route, so preservation depends on owned PC/console media. The PC/PS3/Xbox 360 branch is the main route, while Wii, DS, and mobile versions should be labeled separately.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned PC or console copy. Record platform, region, patch, controller, difficulty, chapter, collectibles/challenges, Kinect/Move/Wii differences if sampled, and whether DS/mobile routes were excluded.

secondary.why: The main archive route is PC/HD console.

all_releases.reason: primary: best capture/fidelity family when owned.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Current access is owned-copy dependent and platform versions differ.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record platform/region and do not merge with Deathly Hallows Part 2.

entries.title: Harry Potter: Wizards Unite
entries.definitive_edition: Historical final live-service documentation; no current official playable build

emulation.notes: Server-dependent AR mobile service; no official offline/emulated route is sourced.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Historical captures and account records only

primary.version: Final live-service build before the January 31, 2022 shutdown
primary.why: Niantic officially closed Harry Potter: Wizards Unite on January 31, 2022, so there is no current official playable route. The archive route is historical: saved footage, screenshots, account data, APK/client records, and contemporary documentation from the final live-service period.
primary.how_to_play: Do not plan a normal playthrough. Archive existing captures/account exports if available, record device/OS/app version/server date, and label any third-party footage or preserved client material as historical evidence rather than a playable official route.

all_releases.fidelity: Sunset AR mobile service; original servers are offline.
all_releases.reason: primary: only original release family, now preserved historically rather than playable.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The live service is gone, so launch/finale events, map state, account state, and social/server behavior cannot be fully replayed.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mark as sunset. Do not present preserved clients, videos, or screenshots as an official playable route.
